messages:
Sam Nguyen: Hey team — customer (ACME) opened a ticket: streaming responses sometimes stop mid‑JSON on our SSE endpoint. They see a bunch of events then the last event is truncated and there's no finish_reason, so their client never considers the stream complete.

Sam Nguyen: Example they pasted from curl: they connect to /v1/streams/generate and get: 
```
data: {
  \"id\": \"req_abc123\",
  \"choices\": [
    {\"delta\": \"Hello\"},
    {\"delta\": \" world\"}
  ]
}
data: {
  \"id\": \"req_abc123\",
  \"choices\": [
    {\"delta\": \"!\"},
    {\"note\": \"final chunk incoming\"}
  ]
data: {
  \"id\": \"req_abc123\",
  \"choices\": [
    {\"delta\": \"\"}
    // stream ends abruptly here, no closing brackets, no finish_reason
```

Sam Nguyen: Client side: they see the stream socket close without final event. Repro is intermittent (happens ~1-3% of streams for them), mostly on longer outputs.

infra-bot: Alert: increased 5xxs on streaming-proxy from 1855554300-1855554400 (source: proxy-01). Attach trace id req_abc123.

Priya Patel: Thanks — can you paste the full request headers (x-request-id, user-agent, region) and a curl -v output? Also need server-side x-ray traces or request-id. Did they use keepalive or a proxy between client and our edge?

Sam Nguyen: Sent curl -v output and x-request-id in the ticket. Key bits:
```
> GET /v1/streams/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> Accept: text/event-stream
> Authorization: Bearer sk-***
> User-Agent: acme-bot/1.2
> x-request-id: req_abc123
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream
< transfer-encoding: chunked
< connection: keep-alive
< x-edge-node: proxy-01
< x-request-id: req_abc123
...streaming data...
* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.example left intact
```

Liam Chen: A few hypotheses: (1) upstream (model runtime) closed socket due to OOM or worker exit, leaving proxy to emit TCP FIN while mid-chunk; (2) proxy/edge had a timeout or aggressive buffer flush and cut connection; (3) client or intermediate load balancer hit its own max idle and RST'd.

Liam Chen: On our side I checked logs for req_abc123 — runtime reported no final flush but no explicit runtime error either. Proxy logs show a ConnectionReset for backend: `upstream read error: connection reset by peer` at 1855554334.

Julia K: If the proxy issues an RST while we're streaming, the final bytes can get lost and clients see malformed/incomplete JSON. That would also explain finish_reason missing since the final JSON event never got sent.

Sam Nguyen: Customer asked: why does this only happen on longer outputs?

Liam Chen: Longer outputs mean more chunks/longer lived connections -> more exposure to flaky network or upstream worker restarts. Also more chance for a final flush to be in flight when a process is torn down.

Priya Patel: Repro steps requested for infra: can someone try a synthetic test that reproduces deterministically? Maybe stream a ~6k token output with periodic small sleeps to simulate long-running response. We need to capture: proxy logs, runtime logs, tcpdump on proxy-01, and the client curl -v.

Sam Nguyen: I'll ask customer for a lightweight repro payload. Meanwhile, here's a simple curl-based repro we used locally:
```bash
curl -v -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\
  \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate\" \\
  -d '{\"model\":\"open-xyz\",\"prompt\":\"repeat \"x\" 6000 times\",\"max_tokens\":3000,\"stream\":true}'
```

Sam Nguyen: When it fails locally I get output like above — last line is partial JSON and then socket closes.

Priya Patel: Actions:
- (Priya) Collect proxy tcpdump and error traces for proxy-01 around 1855554330-1855554350.
- (Liam) Instrument runtime to log last outgoing chunk and flush calls for that request id. Add guard to ensure flush on close.
- (Julia) Add client-side mitigation notes for ACME: retry on truncated final event, treat missing finish_reason as terminal after small timeout and rehydrate with `GET /v1/requests/:id` to fetch final state (if available).

Liam Chen: Quick note on mitigation: we're going to add a final heartbeat SSE event from runtime that is just `data: {\"_final_heartbeat\":true}\n\n` — but that is a bit hacky. Better to harden the proxy so it preserves and forwards FIN flushes and to ensure runtime flushes final chunk before shutting down worker.

Julia K: For immediate customer workaround: we recommended client to implement a 3s post-stream idle timeout — if no finish_reason seen, call our REST status endpoint with the request id. That solved their blocking issue while we investigate root cause.

Sam Nguyen: Customer confirmed workaround worked for a day but they still see occasional failures. They've asked for SLA credit investigation.

Priya Patel: Next update timeline: I'll have network pcap & proxy trace by EOD + initial root cause hypothesis. Liam, prioritize runtime flush instrumentation as hotfix.

Liam Chen: Will do. I'll push a small change to runtime to log `OUTGOING_FLUSH request=req_abc123 bytes_sent=...` and a metrics counter for partial-close events.

infra-bot: Task created: STREAM-1234 reproduce + collect pcap (assignee: Priya).

Sam Nguyen: Cool. I'll keep ACME updated and attach recommended client retries. If anyone finds immediate config in proxy-01 (haproxy/nginx) that would prevent mid-chunk truncation, please post.

Julia K: Also adding note: if customers use intermediate proxies (Cloudflare/AWS LB) ask them to confirm TCP idle/timeouts and to disable external buffering.

Sam Nguyen: Thanks all — will update thread when we have traces.

Priya Patel: Update 2h later: pcap shows repeated `RST` from backend IP 10.20.30.5 at times matching truncated streams. Opening infra incident to investigate persistent backend worker process crashes.

Liam Chen: Follow-up: runtime team found a rare edge-case where the KV cache eviction triggered a synchronous restart of a worker while a flush was in progress. Patch rolling now to defer kill until outstanding flushes complete.

Sam Nguyen: I'll send ACME the root cause and ETA for fix. Marking thread as ongoing until patch finishes rolling.

Julia K: Final note for support playbook: add a troubleshooting checklist for streaming truncation — gather curl -v, x-request-id, proxy logs, pcap, and client retry behavior.

Sam Nguyen: Thanks — closing for now but keeping open until patch is fully rolled.
